text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on December 18 in history.
1398 - Turkish warrior Timur Lenk (Tamurlane) conquered Delhi.
1737 - Antonio Stradivari, Italian violin-maker, died. Noted for their astonishing sound quality, his surviving violins are still unsurpassed.
1779 - Joseph Grimaldi, English actor and dancer, born. His character, white-faced "Joey", was a huge influence on the development of the circus clown.
1787 - New Jersey became the third state in the United States.
1863 - Franz Ferdinand, Archduke of Austria, born. His assassination in Sarajevo in 1914 sparked the chain of events which ignited World War One.
1865 - Slavery was abolished throughout the United States with the ratification of the 13th amendment.
1903 - The U.S-Panama treaty placed the Canal Zone under U.S. control for an annual rent.
1911 - Jules Dassin, U.S. film director, born. Best known for his "Rififi" and "Never on Sunday".

1912 - Charles Dawson discovered fossils known as the "Piltdown Man" on Piltdown common in East Sussex, England, and claimed they were the remains of primitive man. It was later discovered to be a hoax.

1913 - German statesman and chancellor Willy Brandt born. Mayor of West Berlin (1957-66), and chancellor from 1969, he was forced to resign in 1974 following the discovery that an aide was an East German spy. Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1971.
1916 - Betty Grable, U.S. film actress, born. Her popularity reached its peak during World War Two when American GIs chose her as their number one pin-up girl.
1916 - In World War One, the 10-month Battle of Verdun ended after huge loss of life -- 543,000 French and 434,000 German troops were killed in the battle.
1919 - British aviator Sir John Alcock crashed and died. Earlier that year he and fellow Briton Arthur Brown had made the first non-stop transatlantic flight.
1940 - A secret plan issued by Adolf Hitler ordered the German General Staff to prepare for the invasion of Russia under the codename "Operation Barbarossa".
1947 - Steven Spielberg, U.S. film maker, born. His films include "E.T.", "Close Encounters of the Third Kind", "Jurassic Park" and "Schindler's List".
1972 - Uganda nationalised 41 foreign-owned farms and tea estates, of which 34 were British.
1980 - Former Soviet prime minister Alexei Kosygin died of heart failure. He was premier from 1964 until 1980.
1987 - Ivan Boesky, the Wall Street financier who played a key role in the biggest insider trading scheme in U.S. history, was jailed for three years.
1989 - The Soviet Union and the European Community signed a trade and economic cooperation pact which they hailed as opening the way to closer pan-European integration.
1993 - Sam Wanamaker, U.S. actor and director who campaigned to rebuild Shakespeare's Globe Theatre on the River Thames in London, died at 74.
1995 - The United States airlifted its first combat troops to Bosnia to join NATO's biggest military mission.
1995 - Zairean passenger plane crashed in Northern Angola killing 141 people.
